entries.note: PMID 20503261 (DMRR 2010) resolves to Glaesner; quote verbatim in abstract. Dulaglutide is a member; untested opener at 2010 is correct.

Barrington 2011a (PMID 21251179, epub 2011-01-19) quote verbatim; healthy volunteers, sc dulaglutide. Exenatide human insulin secretion public before Glaesner (May 2010), so retro under the target-level rule.
PMID 26308095 (J Med Chem, epub 2015-09-11); minipig i.v. t1/2 46.1 h quote verbatim. Minipig appears in the 209637 PharmR bundle text (9 hits).

entries.rule: Evidence rule 2 (source tiers): peer-reviewed paper with DOI is tier 1
entries.note: Kapitza 2015 (PMID 25475122, epub 2015-01-14) quote verbatim; T2D women, sc semaglutide, predates Lau (Sept 2015): retro and year 2015 hold. source_tier is 2 but a peer-reviewed paper is tier 1.
entries.adjudication_note: Status not in dispute: retrodiction rule (dose is a drug claim; Kapitza Jan 2015 precedes Lau Sept 2015) gives retro. Field fix per Evidence rule 2: peer-reviewed PMID paper is source_tier 1.

entries.note: Glaesner 2010 abstract: 'Half-life in rats and cynomolgus monkeys was 1.5-2 days...' verbatim. Protein modality correct for the Fc fusion.
Barrington 2011a abstract states human t1/2 ~90 h and 'half-life that supports once-weekly dosing' verbatim. Ratio 1.9-2.5x to off_by_2-5x is defensible; same is right.
PMID 34127852 is the danuglipron phase 1 MAD (Nat Med 2021); humanized-mouse sentence verbatim. Using a phase 1 paper as model source is acceptable since it states the model result.

Quote verbatim (JAMA Netw Open 2023, PMID 37213102); NCT03985293 results first posted 2022-06-30, primary HbA1c, confirmed. Possible earlier date: the 2021 MAD paper may report day-28 glucose falls (full text not open; unverified).
Glaesner 2010 diabetic-mouse quote verbatim; untested opener 2010.

EGO (PMID 21251180, epub 2011-01-19) quote verbatim; T2D, sc dulaglutide, unselected. Exenatide (2005) and liraglutide (2009) HbA1c results predate Glaesner 2010: retro correct under target-level rule.

125469 PharmR bundle l.265: 'increase in the incidence of thyroid C-cell adenomas at >0.5 mg/kg (≥7X clinical AUC)'; line-wrapped, near-verbatim. FDA calls human relevance unknown, not species-specific.

Rule 5 (#130): a human null contradicts rodent carcinogenicity only if the regulator calls it species-specific (FDA: relevance unknown) or the dataset is powered for MTC (HR 1.19, 0.37-3.86). Cohort is pooled, mostly non-member liraglutide (rule 12).
entries.adjudication_note: Rule 5 (#130): FDA calls human relevance unknown, not species-specific, and the cohort is unpowered for MTC (HR 1.19, 0.37-3.86), so the human null cannot contradict the rat bioassay.

entries.note: Rybelsus PharmR quote verbatim; dog SNAC-ratio study AnP090703 (code dates it ~July 2009) chose 300 mg SNAC before FIH NCT01037582 (Dec 2009). Untested opener at 2009, class level, correct.

entries.rule: Rule 6 (dating): epub_year is the online date
entries.note: Granhall quote verbatim (PMID 30565096); healthy + T2D, oral. Retro holds: Davies 2017 phase 2 preceded any dog data (Buckley STM 2018-11-14 first). Year 2019 ok via FDA review; but Granhall PubMed entry 2018-12-20, so epub_year 2018.
entries.adjudication_note: Status not in dispute: retrodiction rule (oral semaglutide's own human data preceded the 2019 dog review) gives retro. Field fix per rule 6: Granhall online 2018-12-20, so epub_year 2018.

entries.note: Scott 2016 (PMID 27252175) abstract has the quote verbatim. Opener at first use, 2016, class level.
Quote verbatim in abstract. Class glucose lowering was known a decade before the genetic proxy and the paper compares against it, so retro (decision 10) is right.
Sathananthan 2010 full text (PMC2928367): quote verbatim; Ser168 carriers ~15% lower beta-cell responsivity on GLP-1 infusion. Patient-level opener 2010 correct.
Dawed (PMID 36528349) quote verbatim; PubMed entry 2022-12-18, print Jan 2023, so year/epub 2022 correct. Pooled GLP-1RA cohorts, drug class, sc, unselected T2D fit.
Trulicity PharmR quote verbatim; reviewer states sponsor's hypothesis that humans respond like monkeys not rats, so a stated prediction. Monkey study start date not given; 2014 proxy acceptable.
Trulicity MedR quote verbatim. Mean calcitonin flat vs placebo matches monkey prediction; outlier caveat recorded. Same at class level supported.
Scott 2016 abstract quote verbatim; stated CV-safety prediction. Note: SUSTAIN-6 topline press release (2016-04-28) and LEADER topline (Mar 2016) preceded publication (2016-06-01).

SUSTAIN-6 (PMID 27633186) quote verbatim; sc semaglutide, unselected T2D. Topline press release 2016-04-28 precedes Scott (2016-06-01), so retro by post-dating; drug 'class' allowed for a genetics system.

entries.rule: Retrodiction: for safety the same drug's own earlier patient result makes the model a retrodiction
entries.note: REWIND (PMID 31189511) quote verbatim, sc, unselected. But dulaglutide's own CV-safety meta-analysis (Ferdinand 2016, PMID 26912057, epub 2016-02-24: 'does not increase the risk of major CV events') predated Scott, as did SUSTAIN-6 on this class track.
entries.adjudication_note: Retrodiction rule (safety: same drug's own earlier result): dulaglutide CV-safety meta-analysis (Ferdinand, PMID 26912057, 2016-02-24, no MACE increase) preceded Scott 2016 (June), so REWIND reproduces a known result: retro.

entries.note: Glaesner 2010 (PMID 20503261, May 2010) quote verbatim; 'was well tolerated' in monkeys is a scorable tolerability claim. Untested opener 2010, dulaglutide, sc correct.

EGO conclusion sentence verbatim; nausea/diarrhoea/distension 13.8% at top dose supports partial. No dulaglutide patient tolerability found public before Glaesner, so prospective same; T2D, sc, unselected; OAMs not a combination.

missing: Dose (semaglutide, peptide): earlier patient PK source Kapitza 2015, J Clin Pharmacol, doi:10.1002/jcph.443 (PMID 25475122), and phase 2 dose-finding Nauck 2016 Diabetes Care doi:10.2337/dc15-0165 (epub 2015-09-10); either dates the semaglutide dose comparison to 2015 instead of the 2017 label.

Safety (danuglipron, small molecule, imported_from obesity): Pfizer 2025-04-14 discontinuation after one case of possible drug-induced liver injury in an obesity dose-optimisation study (tier 5; e.g. https://www.cnbc.com/2025/04/14/pfizer-scraps-daily-weight-loss-pill-danuglipron.html). Pfizer says overall liver-enzyme rates matched approved GLP-1 RAs; scorable only if a tier 1-3 tox source states hepatic silence, otherwise untested at most.

No missed efficacy failures found for other members: TTP273 phase 2 positive (vTv 2017, placebo-subtracted HbA1c -0.86/-0.71%), CJC-1134-PC phase 2 HbA1c fell vs placebo (NCT00638716/NCT00674466), efpeglenatide AMPLITUDE programme positive; LY2428757 discontinuation reason not found.

Safety (semaglutide): SUSTAIN-6 headline press release 2016-04-28 (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2016/4/28/1600310/0/en/semaglutide-significantly-reduces-the-risk-of-major-adverse-cardiovascular-events-in-the-sustain-6-trial.html) predates Scott 2016 publication (2016-06-01); the safety 6 confidence_note should record it.
rule_questions: Rule 5/12: when the only human null for an on-target class harm is a pooled cohort in which non-member drugs (here liraglutide) dominate, does it count for the member class at all, or only for the member share, and how is that share recorded?

Rule 7: when the patient source (Kapitza, Jan 2015) predates the publication of the model source (Lau, Sept 2015) but the model was used prospectively before the clinic, is the paired entry dated to the later publication, or to the patient source with the model's use year as proxy?

Safety silence: a single tier-5 liver-injury case in another indication (obesity), which the sponsor says sits at class-background rates. Is that a contradicted silence, or does it need a tier 1-4 patient source before it can be scored?

Ala316Thr genetics (safety 5/6): the analysis was done before, but first published after, the SUSTAIN-6 topline press release (2016-04-28). Decision 10 requires post-dating AND being motivated by the patient result; does first-public date alone make it retro? Scored same here.

Ala316Thr genetics (safety 7): the model predicts both CV safety (no excess) and possible benefit. When a member's own no-harm result (Ferdinand 2016 meta-analysis) predates the model but its benefit result (REWIND superiority) does not, is the later outcome trial a prospective test of the benefit claim or a retrodiction of the safety claim?
